WEB-003.1.title: [WEB-003.1] Configure public WSS URL, trusted forwarding and browser security headers

hardAcceptanceDependencies.why: Deployment consumes a launchable image/bundle, not just renderer static assets.
Trusted forwarding and cookie/WS security must use actual auth assumptions.
Domain/TLS, runtime access and persistence are concrete resources; local reverse proxy tests can start now.

currentImplementation: Explicit public WS URL and Secure-cookie override already exist; embedded WebUI shares HTTP/WS port and supports TLS certificate/key pair. Login rate-limit forwarded IP trust exists when direct socket IP matches trustedProxies.

Existing WebUI proto/host inference reads forwarded headers independently of proxy-IP trust. Node adapter does not preserve a direct socket-IP resolver for createWebuiHandler; standalone entry supplies neither trustedProxies nor resolveClientIp.

WS listener currently attaches WebSocketServer directly to HTTP/HTTPS without explicit allowed-Origin verification. Native auth still rejects unproved actions; origin policy is an additional browser ingress boundary.

sourceFindings.finding: shouldUseSecureCookies and fallback WS URL trust spoofable forwarded proto/host. Rate-limit proxy gate is separate and Node embedded handler has no direct-IP wiring, yielding shared direct key. Explicit Secure=true/publicWSS mitigate deployment URL behavior but do not prove trusted header rejection.

Current WS upgrades have no allowed-Origin policy; current WebUI auth/config/SPA responses have no centralized browser security/header/cache policy. Keep existing path containment and cookie attributes.

Network plain-WS refusal runs after bootstrap/listen and printed ready URL; source Docker defaults non-localhost plain WS and therefore needs direct TLS or explicit private-upstream override. Current smoke treats log URL as readiness and can fall back to port-open success.

WEB-003.2.title: [WEB-003.2] Persist data, credentials, profiles, models and job state

hardAcceptanceDependencies.why: Deployment consumes a launchable image/bundle, not just renderer static assets.
Trusted forwarding and cookie/WS security must use actual auth assumptions.
Domain/TLS, runtime access and persistence are concrete resources; local reverse proxy tests can start now.

currentImplementation: Config directory resolution supports explicit ROX_CONFIG_DIR, then CRAFT fallback, clean ~/.rox, legacy ~/.craft-agent. Source Docker precreates legacy tree and therefore tends to keep legacy default; explicit mount/env avoids ambiguity.

Native authority/journal state defaults inside canonical resolved config/native-data and requires owner/privacy; credentials v3 already preserves master-key custody with keychain or0600 file fallback and recovery/quarantine checks.

Browser manager default profile is hardcoded HOME/.craft-agent/browser-profile, separate from explicit ROX_CONFIG_DIR unless CRAFT_BROWSER_PROFILE is set. Workspace roots stored in config can also be outside mounted config.

sourceFindings.finding: Source image recursively chmod777s home; named/mapped volumes and arbitrary --user need declared UID/GID rather than world-write access. Generated compose mounts /root/.craft-agent but generated clean home may resolve /root/.rox; unlike source Docker it does not precreate legacy tree.

references.reason: Generated root runtime and legacy volume

Copying config.json or persistent mount existence does not establish clean-host credential usability or journal-safe recovery.

Declare every external workspace root, selected tool/model cache and job artifact directory; use fixture readback inventory instead of assuming all paths are under config.

Run non-root with declared UID/GID; create only intended data directories with owner mode0700/credential0600, remove777 home contract via SERVER-BUILD owner, and keep application/code/certificates read-only where compatible.

Back up credential master key separately under declared custody/encryption policy alongside ciphertext, migrations and quarantine receipts. Do not regenerate a missing key and label restored connections healthy.

Use graceful stop/consistent snapshot or database-supported checkpoint/backup for authority/journal/WAL/staging and scheduled jobs; restore receipt must prove authorization/current revision and resumable workflow, not only byte hashes.
